data.title: Biodexa Pharmaceuticals Posts Interim 1H26 Results and Expands GI Cancer Pipeline
data.description:

Operationally, Health Canada approved expansion of the Serenta trial into Canada in June 2026, with 92 of a planned 168 subjects enrolled as of publication, and Fiona Sharp was promoted to CFO and joined the board from January 2026. Post-period, Biodexa raised $3.5 million in gross proceeds through a mix of registered direct, warrant inducement and PIPE offerings, bolstering a cash balance of £3.23 million at June 30, 2026 amid rising R&D spend and continued financing challenges.

data.title: NET Power Restructures Oxy-Combustion Partnership With Baker Hughes
data.description:
The latest update is out from NET Power ( (NPWR) ).

On September 8, 2026, NET Power and Baker Hughes affiliates executed a set of integrated agreements that indefinitely suspend their joint development and commercialization programs for utility-scale oxy-combustion power plants while amending an existing license for industrial-scale applications. The move stems from changing market and economic conditions and NET Power’s conclusion that continuing the specific utility-scale turboexpander and platform programs is not currently economical.

Under the new arrangements, performance under the Amended and Restated Joint Development Agreement and the Commercial Agreement is frozen for an indefinite period, and Baker Hughes’ special access and exclusivity rights over NET Power’s La Porte, Texas demonstration facility are terminated. At the same time, Baker Hughes’ Nuovo Pignone affiliates retain exclusive rights to utility-scale equipment packages and gain revised, largely royalty-based industrial licensing terms, though no party is obligated to deploy plants and no royalty amounts are set or assured.

NET Power preserves ownership of its oxy-combustion intellectual property but remains constrained by Baker Hughes’ exclusivity in utility-scale equipment, limiting its ability to seek alternative manufacturers without further changes to the agreements. The company’s options for the La Porte facility, including continued use, sale or decommissioning, are no longer tied to Baker Hughes’ contractual rights, and previously accrued payments for past work under the joint development program continue to be settled in cash and equity.

The transaction aligns with NET Power’s previously disclosed strategy not to fund further development of the Oxy-Combustion Cycle, following a $193.7 million non-cash impairment recorded in the quarter ended June 30, 2026 that reduced the carrying amount of its developed oxy-combustion technology and the La Porte facility to zero. While the impairment does not affect legal ownership of the technology, future value realization now depends on industrial plants that Baker Hughes’ affiliates or their customers may choose to develop, with no guarantee of such deployments or resulting royalty income.
